title: Remapping CapsLock key to Home causes miscellaneous issues with remote control programs

status.label: Investigate modifier state across remote sessions
status.detail: The report says Caps Lock mapped to Home works initially but, after several remote-control logins, leaves Caps Lock active and other keys such as Enter/Ctrl unusable until PowerToys exits.

judgment.rationale: The report describes a repeatable pattern across multiple computers and two remote-control products: with Caps Lock mapped to Home, the keyboard may become stuck in a Caps Lock-like state after several remote logins, and exiting PowerToys restores normal input. It lists PowerToys 0.94.2 and gives OS, elevation, and remote-client details. This supports investigating synthetic modifier-state cleanup across remote sessions, though the report predates current stable and has no current-build retest.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.2, Windows build 26100, PowerToys running elevated, and a per-machine installation.
The mapping is Caps Lock to Home; an optional Right Shift to End mapping is reported as not relevant.
After several remote logins, letters appear in uppercase, Shift reverses the case, and Enter/Ctrl shortcuts may stop working.
Exiting PowerToys restores normal keyboard behavior.
The author reports the behavior across ARM and Intel computers and with Radmin 3.5.2 and Remote Utilities 7.6.2.
The issue has no comments or assignees.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm the sequence on current stable and trace whether Keyboard Manager leaves a synthesized modifier or key state uncleared across remote-control session transitions.

fix_assessment.rationale: The remapping configuration and PowerToys-exit workaround point to a Keyboard Manager input-state issue across remote sessions. The exact event or client transition causing the stuck state is not established.

proposed_fixes.title: Clear stale remapped key state after remote-control sessions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager may retain a synthesized modifier or key state when remote-control clients change the input stream, leaving Caps Lock or other key state stuck after repeated sessions.
plan: Reproduce with Caps Lock mapped to Home while connecting and disconnecting through Radmin or Remote Utilities over repeated sessions.
Record which physical and synthesized key states remain active when letters, Enter, and Ctrl shortcuts stop working.
Trace the Keyboard Manager remap and key-state cleanup path when remote-control software injects or redirects input.
If a remapped key state remains active across the session transition, clear or reconcile that state on the existing input lifecycle boundary without disrupting normal local remapping.
verification: Repeated remote-control sessions do not leave Caps Lock, Shift, Enter, or Ctrl in a stuck state.
The Caps Lock-to-Home mapping works before and after remote sessions without exiting PowerToys.
Local keyboard input and the optional Right Shift-to-End mapping continue to behave as configured.

confidence.rationale: The failure pattern and PowerToys-exit workaround are detailed and reported across multiple machines and remote clients, but the issue uses 0.94.2 and does not identify which input-state transition becomes stuck.

issue_context.summary: After multiple remote-control logins, a Caps Lock-to-Home mapping reportedly leaves Caps Lock active and other keys unusable until PowerToys exits.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.2 on Windows build 26100, running elevated as a per-machine installation.
The primary mapping is Caps Lock to Home; Right Shift to End is reported as not relevant.
After several remote sessions, letters appear uppercase and Enter/Ctrl shortcuts may stop working.
Exiting PowerToys restores normal keyboard behavior.
The author reports testing across ARM and Intel computers and with Radmin 3.5.2 and Remote Utilities 7.6.2.
inferences: A remapped key or modifier state may remain active when remote-control software changes the input path, but no event trace confirms this.
issue_context.analysis: The multi-client and multi-machine pattern with a PowerToys-exit workaround justifies an input-state investigation. Confirm the failure on current stable and identify which state remains stuck before implementing cleanup behavior.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body, labels, assignees, and discussion; there are no comments or assignees.
The report itself names two remote-control products and multiple computer architectures, so no additional duplicate was needed to justify investigation.

information_gaps.information: Whether the same stuck-key behavior occurs on current stable with the reported Caps Lock-to-Home mapping and repeated remote-control sessions
information_gaps.why_needed: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.2; a current result confirms the failure is still live before tracing input-state cleanup.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the reported sequence on current stable with one remote-control client and confirm whether restarting or exiting PowerToys is still required to restore the keyboard.

actions.label: Confirm the remote-session failure on current stable

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed report across Radmin and Remote Utilities, including the Caps Lock-to-Home mapping and the PowerToys-exit workaround. Since the report lists PowerToys 0.94.2, could you confirm whether the same stuck-key behavior still occurs on current stable after repeated remote-control logins?
